_comment_family: Marydale ships as a family - a Regular and a Black either side of the
Bold this folder holds - and every one of those files carries
'Marydale' as name ID 1, with the cut in the subfamily. Asking for
'Marydale' alone would let any of them answer, and this face is used
as a highlight against a hand of a quite different weight: a Regular
answering in its place would be lighter still, which is the emphasis
further backwards rather than merely different.
So the full name (name ID 4) is what gets declared, the same way
gilroy-extrabold and american-typewriter-itc-pro-bold declare theirs.
The hyphen in it is the font's own: this file writes 'Marydale-Bold'
on both platforms where those two carry a spaced Windows name beside
the PostScript one, and it is left exactly as the file spells it. A
name tidied into 'Marydale Bold' would be a name nothing is installed
under, which is a local() source that can never match and a value the
installer would register the face under while Windows keyed it by
something else (see FONT_FULL_NAME in installer/engine.py).
Weight 700, which is the file's own usWeightClass and what the cut is
called. It is worth knowing that this Bold is LIGHTER on the page than
the 400-weight face it is picked out against - see the highlight note
in hoodsiderz/channel.json, where that is the pairing the channel
chose and not an accident of naming.
_comment_css: Not declared in styles.css: this face arrived with a channel and is
registered from this JSON, which is the route content/README.md
describes. Nothing has to be added to the stylesheet for it.
_comment_local: What the machine may already know the face by, tried after the file,
and one name long rather than the usual two - the PostScript name and
the Windows full name are the same string in this file, so there is no
second spelling to list. It is also what the installer registers the
'Marydale' on its own is deliberately absent: it is the family, and
the Regular and the Black answer to it as well.
_comment_stack: Damage limitation, and the one thing it must not do is fall through to
the same face the block does. This face is a HIGHLIGHT: its whole job
is to be a visibly different hand from Chelsea Market Pro on the same
line, and a stack that ended up at the same substitute would leave a
picked word identical to the words either side of it - a failure that
draws no attention to itself, which is the kind this app has been bitten
So the two hands stay two hands all the way down: Ink Free first, which
is on every Windows 10 and 11 and is a loose marker hand of roughly
this weight, where chelsea-market-pro leads with Segoe Print. Comic
Sans MS is on both lists and is the point at which they converge, which
is one substitution later than it would otherwise have been. Impact and
Arial Black are absent for that pack's reason: they are heavy
grotesques, and nothing about this face is a grotesque.
